outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has acquired one unreviewed OpenAI claim (first public 6 October 2026) that refutes the homeomorphism-existence form in dimension four, a 2024 smooth-category dimension-four counterexample that leaves the topological question untouched, and several restricted-class or boundary partial results, with no accepted resolution of the topological problem.
problem_asks: Bullet: 'Aspherical closed manifolds are determined up to homeomorphism by their fundamental groups.' Parts: (1) for closed aspherical manifolds M and N with isomorphic fundamental groups, M is homeomorphic to N; the bullet does not restrict the dimension, so the claim as worded is universal over dimensions (a failure in one dimension falsifies it as worded). (2) The category is topological (homeomorphism), not smooth or diffeomorphism. (3) The standard stronger formulation, used by Wikipedia and Lueck, asks that every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds be homotopic to a homeomorphism; the bullet states only the existence form, so the two must be kept separate. (4) Implicitly, the question is asked for every fundamental group; the known cases are dimensions 1 and 2 (classification), dimension 3 (geometrisation, per the sources), and higher-dimensional results for restricted groups classes (Farrell-Jones type), dimension 4 only under goodness.

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math release has a first public commit on 6 Oct 2026 (21:58:50 UTC, 'Initial commit', sha adc7f12). It contains preprints/Nonhomeomorphic-closed-aspherical-four-manifolds-with-the-same-homotopy-type-October-4-2026/, with author line 'OpenAI' and a title block dated October 4, 2026. Abstract (read from build/paper.tex): 'We construct closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, disproving the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four. Their common fundamental group is word-hyperbolic. One of the manifolds also has a self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to a homeomorphism.' The theorems are labelled thm:pair (Theorem 1.1) and thm:self-map (Theorem 1.2); the statements as read in the source are given under direction and object. The construction, as read in hyperbolicity.tex: a reflection extension E = W semidirect H with H a nonabelian free group, a locally finite CAT(0) cube complex with proper cocompact E-action, and a common group Pi of finite index in E, shown word-hyperbolic with Out(Pi) finite. The manuscript relies on two same-day OpenAI manuscripts keyed MT and PD in its references (MT = A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding; PD = A PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model), and cites Khan 2012, Bartels-Lueck 2012, Davis 1983 and 2008, Block-Weinberger 2008, and the smooth Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian paper by key only. Secondary trackers list the claim as Disproved (topology index), and as Candidate (review pending), Verification Unreviewed, with no Lean file at the pinned commit (VibeMathed). The manuscript's own title block says October 4; the repository first appears October 6.
events.delivers: If the manuscript is correct, there are closed aspherical topological 4-manifolds M and N, homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with common word-hyperbolic fundamental group Pi (Theorem 1.1). Since aspherical manifolds with the same fundamental group are homotopy equivalent, this refutes the bullet's existence form in dimension four. Theorem 1.2 gives, for one such M, a self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to any homeomorphism, which refutes the stronger homotopy-to-homeomorphism form in that dimension. Restrictions: topological category; dimension four only, as the abstract states; the group is the specific word-hyperbolic Pi built by reflection; the manifolds are obtained through the MT and PD inputs, which I did not read in full. The intro says the cyclic-cover criterion 'works in every manifold dimension', but no counterexample in another dimension is stated in the text I read; a curator summary says nothing is shown in dimensions five or higher (not checked against the TeX).
events.remains: Dimensions 1-3, and dimensions five and higher, are not addressed by any result stated in the manuscript. In dimension four, the statement covers only the constructed group class, so the status for good fundamental groups is not changed by it. The manuscript does not say whether Pi is good in Freedman's sense, and that point is what the dependencies bear on (see doubts).
events.time_since_posted: 5 days as of 11 Oct 2026 (first public 6 Oct 2026)
events.directly_checkable: No object checkable by hand. The claim is a 60-page construction (Davis reflection on a Poincare chamber with a CAT(0) cube complex; Pi with Out(Pi) finite) whose realisation of the manifolds and whose homotopy equivalence come from MT and PD sections I did not read. The 60-page argument would have to be checked section by section.
events.doubts: (1) Unreviewed dependency: the claim stands or falls with the two same-day unreviewed OpenAI manuscripts MT and PD (VibeMathed says so; the references file confirms the dependence). (2) Goodness: the dependency MT, as its boundary-only sibling's abstract states, asserts that the free group on two generators is not good in the sense of Freedman-Quinn, and that the same holds for any group containing it. Pi contains a finite-index subgroup of the nonabelian free group H (hyperbolicity.tex), so under that dependency Pi is not good. Freedman's conjecture that non-abelian free groups are not good is, from my search results, still open (a 2026 Krushkal preprint describes it as open), so the Borel claim rests on a claim in the direction of an open conjecture, and I could not read MT's own body to see the argument. (3) Khan tension: the manuscript cites Khan 2012 for rigidity up to topological s-cobordism for closed aspherical 4-manifolds with torsion-free word-hyperbolic fundamental group (Theorem 1.22 and Corollary 1.23 as the manuscript cites them). Khan's abstract, which I read, gives the dimension-four Borel conjecture 'up to s-cobordism' under Farrell-Jones. A homotopy equivalence that is not homotopic to a homeomorphism is compatible with s-cobordism only where the four-dimensional s-cobordism theorem fails, which is where goodness fails; the manuscript does not spell this out in the text I read. (4) Provenance: no human is named; the author is 'OpenAI'; the manuscript has no disclosure or review statement; the release README says the vast majority of results came from an unreleased internal model and that some unformalised results could have issues. (5) No Lean file exists for this manuscript at the pinned commit (per VibeMathed; I did not inspect lean/ directly).
events.direction: Cuts against the bullet's existence form in dimension four: it exhibits homotopy equivalent, non-homeomorphic closed aspherical 4-manifolds with the same word-hyperbolic fundamental group. Theorem 1.2 also cuts against the stronger homotopy-to-homeomorphism form for one of them.
events.object: Theorem 1.1: a pair of closed connected aspherical topological 4-manifolds M and N with common word-hyperbolic fundamental group Pi, homotopy equivalent but with no homeomorphism between them, the conclusion excluding every homeomorphism without prescribing a homotopy class. Pi is a finite-index subgroup of a reflection extension E = W semidirect H, H a nonabelian free group, W acting cocompactly and properly on a CAT(0) cube complex built by a support construction; Out(Pi) is finite and Pi has one end and no splitting over a virtually cyclic subgroup. Theorem 1.2: for one of these M, a homotopy equivalence f: M to M such that no homeomorphism M to M is homotopic to f. Constructive at the group level; the manifolds and the homotopy equivalences are obtained through the realisation and surgery inputs of MT and PD, which I did not read, so I cannot say they are explicit.

events.what_happened: OpenAI release manuscript 'A PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model' (title block dated September 24, 2026; first public appearance is the repository commit of 6 Oct 2026). Abstract (read from build/paper.tex): 'We construct a finitely presented integral Poincare duality group of dimension four that has a finite classifying space but is not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical topological four-manifold. This gives a negative answer to Wall's manifold-realization question in dimension four.' The body is said to refute the assertion quantified over all n at least 3, without asserting a counterexample in every dimension. The manuscript is cited as PD by the Borel manuscript (reflection and realisation results; controlled filling; support construction, Lemma 3.3). It names as its starting point the marked tensor obstruction MT, and cites Kasprowski-Land four-dimensional surgery and Farrell-Jones via a CAT(0) action; it says it replaces the goodness-dependent null-loop step of Powell-Ray-Teichner. The topology index calls the same result 'disproving Wall's conjecture'.
events.delivers: A finitely presented PD4 group with a finite classifying space that is not the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological 4-manifold; a negative answer to Wall's realisation question in dimension four for finitely presented groups.
events.remains: Wall's realisation question in other dimensions, and for groups not finitely presented. Nothing about homeomorphism of aspherical manifolds with a given fundamental group, so the Borel bullet is not addressed directly.
events.time_since_posted: 5 days as of 11 Oct 2026 (first public 6 Oct 2026)
events.doubts: It depends on MT, which I could not read (only its preamble was readable through the fetch tool). The paper's own chain of inputs (Kasprowski-Land, Farrell-Jones via CAT(0), Davis-Hillman realisation) is cited, not reproduced, in the sections I could read. Unreviewed.
events.direction: Cuts against Wall's realisation question in dimension four for finitely presented PD4 groups; it does not directly answer the Borel bullet. It enters the Borel claim as an input (PD).
events.object: A finitely presented group G, with a finite oriented four-dimensional aspherical Poincare complex Q, such that H^i(G; ZG) vanishes for i not equal to 4 and is Z for i = 4, but no closed aspherical topological four-manifold has fundamental group G. The manuscript's chamber has nonabelian free fundamental group, and its marked filling obstruction is stated to concern the four-dimensional case outside the elementary amenable hypothesis (quoted sentence fragments from the PD body as fetched).

events.what_happened: Vyacheslav Krushkal, '4-manifold topology and collision rank of groups', arXiv 21 Sep 2026 (single version). Abstract (read): introduces 'collision rank', shows groups of finite collision rank are good in the sense of topological 4-manifold theory, and gives finitely generated examples of collision rank two outside the subexponentially amenable groups (commutator subgroups of topological full groups of Sturmian systems, including continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic infinite simple amenable groups).
events.delivers: Goodness (in the Freedman sense) for the class of groups of finite collision rank. This is a new class of good groups; it does not say that any closed aspherical manifold is determined by its fundamental group.
events.remains: The Borel question for these groups is not addressed by the abstract; any dimension-four consequence would go through the standard reduction for good groups, which the OpenAI manuscript describes as assuming goodness (Bartels-Lueck Proposition 0.3 as cited there). Nonabelian free groups are not addressed by the abstract as read.
events.direction: Consistent with the bullet's direction for a new class of good groups in dimension four, where goodness is the hypothesis under which rigidity is known. It is not a direct resolution.

events.what_happened: Ioannis Gkeneralis, 'Remarks on Topological Rigidity of Real Moment-Angle Manifolds', arXiv 2604.15462, single version submitted 16 Apr 2026 (11 pages). Claims that real moment-angle manifolds associated to flag simplicial complexes, of dimension at least five, satisfy the Borel conjecture. The HTML text states that the real moment-angle complex is aspherical if and only if K is a flag complex (Corollary 2.5), and that the Davis complex is CAT(0) (so the group satisfies Farrell-Jones), and then applies surgery theory (Lemma 4.2, Theorem 4.3). It also says the complex and quaternionic analogues are not aspherical (Lemmas 2.6, 2.7).
events.delivers: Borel rigidity (every homotopy equivalence to such an aspherical manifold is homotopic to a homeomorphism) for the class of real moment-angle manifolds of flag complexes, dimension at least five.
events.remains: All other closed aspherical manifolds, and all other dimensions. My reading, which the judging pass should check: Bartels-Lueck (2012) already covers closed aspherical manifolds of dimension at least five whose fundamental group acts properly and cocompactly on a finite-dimensional CAT(0) space, so this paper's new input is the CAT(0) identification of the group, and its Borel conclusion appears to be an instance of that earlier theorem.
events.directly_checkable: Real moment-angle manifolds of flag complexes are explicit cubical manifolds; their asphericity is stated to follow from the flag condition.
events.direction: Consistent with the bullet's direction on a class: determined up to homeomorphism by the fundamental group within that class.

events.what_happened: James F. Davis and J. A. Hillman, 'Aspherical manifolds with boundary', arXiv 2501.12509, v1 21 Jan 2025 (21:41:34 UTC), v2 29 Jun 2026 (comment: 'New title. Added Conjecture B, which gives a homological criterion for the homotopy type of a compact aspherical manifold'). A search summary gives the v1 title as 'The Borel Conjecture for manifolds with boundary'; I did not open v1. Abstract (read): a homological criterion for when a closed manifold, with maps from its components' fundamental groups, can be the boundary of a compact aspherical manifold, proved by building a Poincare pair and applying surgery; illustrated for abelian fundamental groups; a sequel classifies compact aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group. The closed case is referred to but not proved here.

events.what_happened: James F. Davis and J. A. Hillman, 'Aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group', arXiv 2501.12512, v1 21 Jan 2025 (21:50:05 UTC), v2 29 Jun 2026 ('Minor rewrites and corrections'). Abstract (read): classifies possible elementary amenable fundamental groups of compact aspherical 4-manifolds with nonempty boundary (polycyclic or solvable Baumslag-Solitar); because these groups are good and satisfy Farrell-Jones, such manifolds satisfy topological rigidity relative to the boundary (a homotopy equivalence that is a homeomorphism on the boundary is homotopic rel boundary to a homeomorphism); classifies the closed 3-manifolds that bound them; two such manifolds are homeomorphic exactly when their enhanced peripheral group systems are equivalent. A Notre Dame talk (29 Apr 2025, 'The Borel Conjecture for compact aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group', read in the seminar page) describes this as proving the Borel conjecture for all compact aspherical 4-manifolds with boundary whose fundamental group is good.
events.delivers: Borel-type rigidity for compact aspherical 4-manifolds with nonempty boundary and elementary amenable (hence good) fundamental group, relative to the boundary; classification of boundaries and of such manifolds up to homeomorphism. The closed statement is not proved here.
events.remains: The closed case in dimension four and all other dimensions, as bulleted. The paper's own abstract restricts to compact manifolds with boundary.
events.direction: Consistent with the bullet's direction, restricted to compact manifolds with boundary and good groups. Not a closed-case result.

Journal reference: Journal of Topology and Analysis (online December 2016; DOI 10.1142/S1793525318500139). Abstract (read, verbatim fragments): the simple Borel conjecture (in dimensions at least five) holds for every group of the form G semidirect Z, where G is Farrell-Jones; the bordism Borel conjecture holds for G semidirect Z, with the extra hypothesis Wh(G times Z) = 0.
events.delivers: Simple Borel (dimensions at least five) for semidirect products G semidirect Z with G Farrell-Jones; bordism Borel under Whitehead-group vanishing.
events.remains: The unrestricted Borel statement; groups not of this form; dimensions below five.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the article (per arXiv journal reference)

events.direction: Consistent with the bullet's direction, for a class of groups in dimensions at least five, in a simple form.

disputes.summary: The status labels for the OpenAI dimension-four claim conflict across trackers: VibeMathed gives Result 'Disproved' with Status 'Candidate (review pending)' and Verification 'Unreviewed'; the topology index says the result disproves the homeomorphism-existence formulation. The manuscript itself carries no status, and no journal or referee record exists.

Two different refutations are both called 'the Borel conjecture fails in dimension four'. Davis et al. (2024) refute the smooth analogue (homeomorphic, not diffeomorphic), which leaves the topological bullet untouched. The OpenAI claim refutes the homeomorphism form. A 2026 aggregator and a blog commenter conflate them; the homeomorphic-not-diffeomorphic result is not the one the OpenAI claim asserts.

The topology index calls the PD manuscript 'disproving Wall's conjecture'. The manuscript's abstract says 'a negative answer to Wall's manifold-realization question in dimension four', and its body refutes the assertion quantified over all dimensions n at least 3 without a counterexample in each dimension.

The manuscripts list OpenAI as sole author and name no human. The release README attributes the vast majority of results to an unreleased internal OpenAI model. Coverage reports that the prompts, the model name and per-problem compute were withheld. No human is credited with the mathematics of the Borel manuscript.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 the problem has moved in three ways, and none of them is an accepted resolution of the topological bullet. (1) The one event that bears on the bullet as worded is OpenAI's release, first public on 6 October 2026 (manuscript title block dated 4 October), of a 60-page claim that there are closed aspherical topological 4-manifolds, homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group, which would refute the homeomorphism-existence form in dimension four. I read its abstract, theorem labels, introduction, hyperbolicity section and references from the openai/math source. Its author line is 'OpenAI'; it has no disclosure, review statement or Lean file; the topology index labels it Disproved while VibeMathed labels it Candidate (review pending) and Unreviewed. It rests on two same-day OpenAI manuscripts keyed MT and PD: PD's abstract and main theorem I read, and its starting point is MT, whose body I could not read. The chain's weak point is goodness. The dependencies assert that the free group on two generators is not good in Freedman-Quinn's sense (the boundary-only sibling's abstract, which I read, states it), and Pi contains a finite-index nonabelian free subgroup, so Pi would be non-good. Freedman's conjecture that free groups are not good is, by my search results, still open, so the claim rests on a claim in the direction of an open conjecture. Khan's 2012 result, which the manuscript cites, gives dimension-four rigidity only up to s-cobordism under Farrell-Jones; that is compatible with a non-homeomorphism only where goodness fails, and the manuscript does not spell out this step in the text I read. (2) Davis, Hayden, Huang, Ruberman and Sunukjian (arXiv 28 Nov 2024; Annals vol. 204, 2026) construct closed aspherical smooth 4-manifolds that are homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic; this refutes only the smooth analogue and is consistent with the topological bullet. (3) Restricted partial results: Davis and Hillman's two January 2025 preprints (boundary versions: compact aspherical 4-manifolds with elementary amenable fundamental group are rigid relative to the boundary, and a homological criterion for compact aspherical manifolds with boundary); Gkeneralis (16 April 2026) on real moment-angle manifolds of flag complexes in dimension at least five, which I read as an instance of Bartels-Lueck (2012) since the group is CAT(0); and Krushkal (21 Sept 2026) showing groups of finite collision rank are good, which bears on dimension four only through goodness. The Aria paper (October 2025) gives a Lean statement of the homotopy form for closed aspherical manifolds ending in sorry, which is a statement, not a proof. I list the older partial results as events because the status is worked out from events: Farrell-Jones 1989, Hsiang-Wall 1969 (not opened), Roushon 2007 (withdrawn 19 July 2007 after Lueck and Linnell found a gap in Lemma 3.8), Bartels-Lueck (2009 arXiv; Annals 2012), Guentner-Tessera-Yu 2010 (stable form), Frigerio-Lafont-Sisto 2011, Barcenas et al. 2015, Khan 2009, and Wang 2015. Checking: no mathematician has publicly checked the OpenAI claim, five days after it appeared; one commenter on a compilation blog states the consequence without checking. On AI involvement: the release README, the authors' own account of the collection, says the vast majority of results came from one fixed procedure with an unreleased internal OpenAI model; this manuscript's text says nothing about its production, so the claim that the model produced this manuscript's mathematics is an inference from the release-level statement. The Davis et al., Davis-Hillman, Gkeneralis and Krushkal papers name no system in the parts I read. Aria's authors disclose that LLMs helped prepare their manuscript, with Gemini-2.5-Pro as a language editor; that is writing help, not mathematics. My reading of close calls: on whether the OpenAI claim settles the bullet in dimension four, the evidence is a claim with unreviewed inputs, not a verified result.
competing_reading: The OpenAI manuscript can be read as a real dimension-four counterexample to the bullet. Its group is word-hyperbolic, Farrell-Jones applies to it, and the known four-dimensional rigidity (Khan, Bartels-Lueck) needs goodness or stops at s-cobordism, so a non-good word-hyperbolic group is exactly where a non-homeomorphic homotopy-equivalent pair could sit. On that reading the homeomorphism-existence form is refuted in dimension four, and so is the homotopy-to-homeomorphism form for one of the manifolds, whatever becomes of the dependencies' fate. The opposite reading: the claim is unreviewed; it depends on two same-day unreviewed manuscripts; its key input is a non-goodness claim in the direction of Freedman's open conjecture; and the manuscript as read does not show why its non-good group avoids Khan's s-cobordism result, so no result has been established on the present record.
what_would_settle_it: Independent checking by four-manifold topologists of: (a) the claim that the free group on two generators is not good, in MT and in the boundary-only manuscript, and its compatibility with the Freedman-Quinn literature; (b) the construction in Sections 3-5 of the Borel manuscript, which produces M, N and the homotopy equivalence from the MT and PD inputs; (c) whether the group Pi of Theorem 1.1 is good, and how Khan's s-cobordism result is avoided. Also: a public response from the Davis/Hillman or Bartels-Lueck circle; a Lean formalisation of the key lemmas, since none exists for this manuscript; and a statement from OpenAI about who wrote or verified the argument and how it was produced.

dead_ends: No accepted or refereed resolution of the topological bullet found anywhere in the sources searched.

No AI-lab claim about the Borel conjecture other than the OpenAI release found; no Gemini, AlphaEvolve or Claude claim about aspherical manifolds found (the Claude and Gemini hits concern the Jacobian conjecture, Erdos problems and Kakeya).
Annals listing for the Davis et al. paper returned HTTP 404; not read.
Hajlasz OpenAI Math catalogue (sites.pitt.edu) exceeds the fetch size limit; not read.
OpenAI's own primary release post was not found by search; the release was described only through secondary coverage and the repository.

The repository's CONTENTS.md and the preprints listing are longer than the fetch tool returns; I read only the visible portions, and family 320 is confirmed only through the topology index and the manuscript directory itself.

The PDFs of the OpenAI manuscripts are compressed and not readable through the fetch tool; their TeX sources were read instead, but only where the source files were present (the MT source gave only the preamble).
Tao blog, Quanta, MathOverflow: searched; no post about the Borel conjecture found.

Carlsson-Goldfarb finite-decomposition-complexity result: appeared in results; the Goldfarb slides (2018) were not opened, and the primary Carlsson-Goldfarb paper was not located.
Lueck's 2025 survey on the Farrell-Jones conjecture (arXiv 2507.11337): appeared in results; not opened, so not used as an event or as evidence about the Borel status.

Expert reactions to the OpenAI Borel claim: searched by name (Davis, Hillman, Agol, Lueck, Tao). The only topology-adjacent reaction found is a reader comment on the Proofs and Prompts compilation (attributed to Xiaolei Wu, a group theorist, in the compilation), which states the consequence without checking it. Ian Agol's comment in the same compilation is general and does not address this result.

Quotations taken from pages read through the fetch tool were produced by that tool and were not byte-checked against the source (the README sentence and the Aria LLM-disclosure paraphrase in particular); the Aria LLM disclosure is quoted from the fetch summary and not verbatim. The Sutherland and Tao reactions, the Scientific American, Nature and Futurism coverage, the Moonlight AI summary, and the Pith pages were seen only in search results and are not used as sources. The claim that the Borel manuscript's theorems hold in every dimension, or that a curator summary says nothing is shown in dimensions five or higher, was not checked in the TeX. The free-group goodness status rests on search summaries (Freedman's conjecture reported as open), not on a source I opened in full.
